title: Theo and Fern's Fossil Find
markdown:
The sun cracked over the garden hedge, pink and gold. Theo the workshop helper stretched. “A new day!” Boots tapped a quick beat on the dew-kissed path. Dewdrops sparkled like diamonds.

Fern the hedgehog sniffed the old stone wall. “Theo! Look!” Her voice trilled with urgency.

Theo dashed over and peered at the rough stone. Strange wavy marks were etched deep, like giant flat footprints. No animal tracks followed. Odd.

“Whose steps?” Fern whispered. “And why no fresh ones?”

Theo tapped his chin. Hard as rock. Impossibly old. “A total puzzle.”

Captain Elowen, the wise robin, landed above. “Ah, little friends. You’ve found a secret from long ago.”

“A secret?” Fern puffed her quills.

“Fossils. Stony echoes of creatures from millions of years before my great-great-great-grand-bird flew.”

Theo blinked. “Millions of years? How did they stay?”

“Picture this.” Captain Elowen’s voice was a lively melody. “A soft mud patch. A creature steps in, leaving a print. More mud and sand tumble down, covering it. Over ages, earth’s weight turns mud to rock. The imprint is preserved. A stony photograph.”

Fern gasped. “Ancient footprints that never faded?”

“Exactly. They tell grand stories of life. This one—” she pointed—“might be from a webbed foot. It suggests this spot was once a marsh.”

Theo’s mind raced. “Fern, I have an idea!” He dashed to his workshop and returned with a flat stone. Fern patted damp mud beside the wall.

They did not rush the press. Theo held the stone above the mud and felt how cool the morning still was. Fern’s nose twitched at wet earth that smelled nothing like rock and everything like now. Then: “Let’s try it!” He pushed the stone in, pressing hard. “Impressions!” Fern nudged her spiky foot, leaving a patterned mark. They imagined earth’s weight and time’s march, which was a lot to imagine before breakfast.

Captain Elowen watched, pleased. “You grasp the principle. Pressure, covering, slow change—nature’s record.”

Theo looked at their muddy creations, then the ancient imprints. “A whisper from the past?”

“Fossils are Earth’s memory. A spectacular library in stone. What do you suppose happened millions of years ago?”

Theo and Fern nodded, minds buzzing. The wall kept its wavy secret and also, now, two new messy ones that would not last millions of years, which was all right. What other pages of that stony library were hiding in ordinary gardens, waiting for a hedgehog’s nose and a workshop helper’s chin-tap?
characters: Theo (workshop helper), Fern (urgent-sniffing hedgehog), Elowen (wise robin captain)
